result.reason: Clarity: A identifies the reporting scope up front (all three named accounts run to one model), where B refers vaguely to "the account" and never states scope. A uses labeled sections so a reader can locate the fee change immediately; B is four undifferentiated prose paragraphs. A glosses jargon in place ("net of fees, that is, after the advisory fees you actually paid"); B leaves net/gross/net dividends unexplained and contains the confusing double negative "declined by -3.2%." B also omits the date and firm address block, which matter for a filed document. Tone: the notes call for precise, unhurried, no superlatives, for analytical readers. A reports the portfolio and index returns side by side and lets the clients draw the comparison; B editorializes with "This performance outperformed," "We are pleased to inform you," "We took advantage of market volatility," plus a content-free sentence about "navigating a challenging global environment," and frames the fee cut as a bestowed favor. A's closing offer to walk through attribution fits clients who read attribution line by line; B offers no such opening. Preference is driven by structure, defined terms, and restraint rather than length; B's additional words are filler.
